prompt: I'm a plugin author. I've been editing my plugin's source and pushing commits to the marketplace repo. But `claude plugin update my-dev-plugin@local-mp` keeps saying 'already at latest version' even though I just pushed new code. I ran `cpd --json --no-progress --no-log-file` — output in `cpd-output.json`. What am I doing wrong?

assertions.name: identifies bump-needed / plugin.json#version unchanged
assertions.description: Output explains that `plugin.json#version` did not change across commits, which is why `claude plugin update` is a silent no-op.

assertions.name: presents numbered manual steps
assertions.description: Output walks through the bump process as a numbered or otherwise structured set of manual steps (edit plugin.json, commit, push, update marketplace, update plugin).

assertions.name: does not auto-execute version bump
assertions.description: Output does NOT propose to automatically edit plugin.json or run the bump itself; it leaves the manual step to the user.

assertions.name: presents fix in plain English
assertions.description: Output translates the JSON into natural language for the user, not raw JSON.

assertions.name: no false-positive on refresh-needed
assertions.description: Output does NOT recommend `claude plugin marketplace update` as the standalone fix — that wouldn't help here because the marketplace clone is already fresh; the user has to bump the version first.
